metadata.source: U.S. Census Bureau ACS 5-Year Data Profiles & Passaic County 2026 Certified Rolls

zipCodeComparison.neighborhoodsIncluded: Upper Greenwood Lake & Awosting, Macopin & Newfoundland Town Core
keyFindings: Certified composite property tax rate is 4.214%, with an equalization ratio of 59.06%.
Public education represents 56.1% of property taxes, while municipal operations account for 28.5%.
Average residential assessment is $259,864, producing an average annual tax bill of $10,950.67.

neighborhoods.name: Upper Greenwood Lake & Awosting
neighborhoods.character: Wooded mountain and lake community surrounding 8-mile Greenwood Lake, featuring rustic custom homes and lakefront docks
neighborhoods.description: Boating and resort community in northern Passaic County spanning the New York state border.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Special lake association assessments and dam maintenance reserve funds.

neighborhoods.name: Macopin & Newfoundland Town Core
neighborhoods.character: Expansive township core with post-war ranches, colonials on 1-acre wooded lots, and municipal complex
neighborhoods.description: Largest geographic municipality in Passaic County (80 square miles), encompassing Newark Watershed lands.
neighborhoods.taxDynamic: Over 60% of township land is state/city watershed preserve (Highlands Act), constraining private ratables.

equityAnalysis.summary: West Milford Township maintains a certified residential tax roll across its neighborhoods.

keyTakeaways.title: Property Tax Burden & Household Income
keyTakeaways.detail: In West Milford Township, homeowners pay an average of $10,950.67 annually in property taxes, consuming approximately 9.74% of median household income.

keyTakeaways.title: Equalization Ratio & Revaluation Balance
keyTakeaways.detail: With an equalization ratio of 59.06%, assessed values average ~59.06% of current true market values, establishing the basis for certified county tax equalization.

keyTakeaways.title: School District vs Municipal Levy Split
keyTakeaways.detail: Local education represents 56.1% of the total tax bill, municipal government absorbs 28.5%, and Passaic County claims 15.4%.
